nested.Name: Application Security Verification Standard Project
nested.Description: The Application Security Verification Standard is a list of application security requirements that architects, developers, testers, security professionals, tool vendors, and consumers can use to define, build, test, and verify secure applications.

Items.Description: Verify that input is decoded or unescaped into a canonical form only once, it is only decoded when encoded data in that form is expected, and that this is done before processing the input further, for example it is not performed after input validation or sanitization.

cdx_levels.description: This level contains the minimum requirements to consider when securing an application and represents a critical starting point.

ASVS Level 2 requirements generally relate to either less common attacks or more complicated protections against common attacks. They may still be a first layer of defense, or they may require certain preconditions for the attack to be successful.

ASVS Level 3 should be the goal for applications looking to demonstrate the highest levels of security and requirements in this section are generally either defense-in-depth mechanisms or other useful but hard-to-implement controls.
